- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.15) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–3% upward bias for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.10), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average if price deviates > 2% from it.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate if recent sentiment is negative and price is consolidating; add 1–4% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
